facts.fact: MyJoyOnline reported on 29 October 2025 that ongoing disruptions in LHIMS had forced some hospitals to revert temporarily to manual record-keeping, after the vendor's contract expired on 31 December 2024 with only 450 of 950 contracted facilities connected.

The Ministry of Health introduced the Ghana Health Information Management System (GHIMS) on 29 October 2025 to replace LHIMS across public health facilities, the Health Minister saying the country would not go back to manual records.

The Health Minister said the LHIMS software was not owned by the state and its cloud infrastructure was hosted in India, under a $100 million contract signed in 2019 with Lightwave to connect 950 facilities, extended to 31 December 2024, on which about $77 million had been paid for 450 facilities.
Announcing GHIMS on 29 October 2025, the Health Minister said the Ministry of Health was 'taking full control' of the health information platform that replaces the vendor-owned LHIMS.

systems.owner: Lightwave (vendor); software not owned by the state
systems.tiers: 450 of 950 contracted health facilities connected; hospitals named, tiers otherwise not stated

note: LHIMS is classed emr on the minister's statement that it held Ghanaians' electronic medical records; GHIMS is classed emr as its stated replacement.
